items.title: The Chinese Adventure 2014: Beijing – Part Two
items.summary: On day three in Beijing I checked out a place known as 798…
items.content_html:
On day three in Beijing I checked out a place known as 798 Art Zone or 798 Art District if you’re a local, and as you can see it’s jam-packed full of some the coolest sculptures on the planet, not only this but the whole site used to be a military factory about 50 years ago leaving some great historic buildings dotted around to snap away with your camera (there’s even an old locomotive!). I also visited the Summer Palace unfortunately but not uncommon here, the smog had got really bad so proved difficult to get the snaps I envisioned but still got a few lucky breaks!

items.title: The Chinese Adventure 2014: Beijing – Part One
items.summary: I catch a bullet train from Shanghai to Beijing and on my…
items.content_html:
I catch a bullet train from Shanghai to Beijing and on my second day I take the advice of a Chinese passenger from the train who told me “Don’t waste the clear skies!” so I arrange a day trip with a taxi driver to The Great Wall of China, the Mutianyu section which I read is less busy than the popular Badaling part, and was rewarded with clear skies and virtually having the wall to myself! In the next few days I also visited The Forbidden City, Beijing Olympic Park, The Temple of Heaven, The CCTV headquarters building and Beihai Park.

items.title: The Chinese Adventure 2014: Shanghai
items.summary: After a 12 hour flight from Heathrow to Hong Kong, then a…
items.content_html: After a 12 hour flight from Heathrow to Hong Kong, then a connecting 2 hour flight to Shanghai I start my China adventure by taking the Maglev train (which uses magnetic levitation to get along with a top speed of 430km/h) into the city and for the next couple of days visit sights such as The Bund Waterfront, The Old Town & Yu Yuan Garden, the view at night from the World Financial Center and I also took part in a Traditional Tea Ceremony!

items.title: The Chinese Adventure 2014: Hong Kong – Part Two
items.summary: The view from Victoria Peak in Hong Kong is famous worldwide, it’s…
items.content_html: The view from Victoria Peak in Hong Kong is famous worldwide, it’s just one of those things you can’t miss when you come over here, and you’re need a pretty decent camera to get the right night time shot (I didn’t quite get what I was hoping for here but I’m still happy with the result). On my second to last day I took the high speed catamaran to the island of Macau, this place is like a mini Las Vegas! Plenty of cool camera opportunities here, crazy majestic buildings, sounds and lights, was a great way to finish what has been an awesome trip! China ~ the size, the culture, the history! ~ this is a truly remarkable country that looks up to no other country, it stands alone in the world, what a great privilege it has been to visit it.

items.title: The Chinese Adventure 2014: Hong Kong – Part One
items.summary: After a long 12 hour coach ride from Guilin, getting through passport control…
items.content_html: After a long 12 hour coach ride from Guilin, getting through passport control in Shenzhen, I was finally on the last metro train to Hong Kong, got to my hotel in Kowloon and hit the sack. Next day I visited the Central Business District (CBD) and was greeted by the sea of protesters tents covering the streets, things had almost died down here but the protesters weren’t giving up that easily. Luckly for me this gave an interesting spin on the photography side of things so I got snapping away and checked out what was happening then walked up to Causeway Bay to catch the classic tram. Next few days was full of checking out this amazing city & also a trip to see the Tian Tan Buddha, serious bit of bronze statue! and at night I watched the Symphony of Lights show on the Victoria Harbour.

items.title: The Chinese Adventure 2014: Yangshuo County
items.summary: Flying out of Chengdu and now arriving into the beautiful countryside of Yangshuo…
items.content_html: Flying out of Chengdu and now arriving into the beautiful countryside of Yangshuo County, Southern China and you get the feel for how big this country is! different terrain, climate, attitudes etc. The relaxed pace of things here was a welcome break and the Phoenix Pagoda Fonglou Retreat is one of the best accommodations I’ve ever stayed in, it was more like living in the home of a Chinese family, Lily and the all the staff were amazing ~ if you ever visit the Yangshuo area I couldn’t recommend this place enough! The main reason I wanted to visit here was actually a photo I saw on the web from one of my favourite photographers, Trey Ratcliff, it was of Laozhai Mountain and I knew I just had to see this amazing place!

items.title: The Chinese Adventure 2014: Chengdu – Part Two
items.summary: One of my other reasons for including Chengdu on my trip (apart…
items.content_html:
One of my other reasons for including Chengdu on my trip (apart from the Giant Buddha) was to visit the Chengdu Panda Breeding & Research Center, organising a trip with the hotel I got there early one morning to catch the pandas meal times, I still remember seeing the very first one amongst all the bamboo trees sitting there like a baby and chewing away on their favourite pastime, just like the one in the photo, brilliant. The rest of my time in Chengdu I spent wandering around the big city and seeing what interesting stuff I could find, I noticed the ‘new found wealth’ China creeping in with old buildings being knocked down and modern ones being put up…

items.title: The Chinese Adventure 2014: Chengdu – Part One
items.summary: The Wenjun Mansion, the hotel I was staying in, and in fact…
items.content_html:
The Wenjun Mansion, the hotel I was staying in, and in fact all the other buildings in the same street were spectacular structures to see and appreciate coming from an ancient time, this theme also carried on with the Kuanxiangzi Alley just around the corner which dates back to the Qing Dynasty (1644 – 1911 AD).

items.title: The Chinese Adventure 2014: Leshan
items.summary: Upon arriving at my accommodation in Chengdu, I enquired about the weather…
items.content_html:
Upon arriving at my accommodation in Chengdu, I enquired about the weather conditions as it was pretty smoggy outside and I wanted to see the Leshan Giant Buddha on the clearest day I had here, at reception they told me that this was gonna be the best day so without even checking in I was off on a two hour coach ride to Leshan to see this extraordinary sight that I’ve dreamt about for the last 6 months ~ and after seeing the Buddha in all his glory I was not disappointed!
